title: Best Voice Over Artists (2026): How to Hire the Right Voice
description: How to hire a voice over artist: pricing by word count, usage rights, audio formats, AI versus human voices, and how to prepare your script.
intro: The right voice makes an explainer, ad or audiobook feel professional within seconds. Voice over gigs are simple to order, but pricing, usage rights and script changes trip up many buyers. This guide shows what to check and how to get a clean recording the first time.

faq.a: Most gigs price by word count, for example per 100 or 150 words, with extras for faster delivery, extra editing or broader usage rights. Count the words in your final script before comparing sellers.

faq.q: Can I use the recording in paid ads or on TV?
faq.a: Check the gig. Many artists include online and organic use by default and charge more for paid advertising, radio or TV. Confirm the usage in writing before ordering.

faq.q: Is the voice human or AI?
faq.a: AI voice services are usually listed separately. If you want a human performance, make sure the gig clearly states the recording is done by the artist, and listen to unedited samples.

faq.q: Can I get a sample of my own script?
faq.a: Many artists will record a short line of your script, sometimes for free. It is the best way to hear how they handle your tone and pronunciation.

faq.q: What if I change the script after recording?
faq.a: Fixing a mistake the artist made is normally free. Changing your own script usually counts as new work. Finalize the script before ordering.
